In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transnational capital is attracted to countries with more transparent and democratic institutions, which have a more liberal economic policy environment.

transnational portfolio investments do not only depend on the economic policies and political institutions of the receiving country, but are also influenced by the economic and political policies of sending countries, as well as international connections.
the ‘race to the bottom’, at least for portfolio investment, is not a zero sum game.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more democratic and transparent a country is, the more attractive it will be to foreign investors, and thus the more foreign investment it will receive.
the more democratic the country, the more transparent it is, and the lower the level of economic intervention in its economy, the more capital will be attracted to it.
investors do care about the quality of economic policies as well as political institutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ‘race to the bottom’, if it exists at all, is not a race between all economies but a competition between economies of similar levels of economic and political development.
political institutions matter and that the nature of political systems is important for the flow of transnational capital.
economic policies are not the only factor that matters in the decision of where to invest, but political institutions also play an important role in attracting transnational portfolio investments.
